title: A Survey on IoT-Enabled Home Automation Systems: Attacks and Defenses
domain: IoT-enabled home automation security (attacks and defenses)

analysis_policy.exclude_scope: References, author bios/photos, acknowledgments, appendix, nomenclature
analysis_policy.notes: Stop before references; span tags retained as markers.

section_flow.objective: Motivate HA security problem, highlight TAP/cross-platform risks, position gap vs prior surveys, state contributions and roadmap.
key_components: Why HA growth increases attack surface
Related survey comparison showing missing attack+defense coverage
notable_moves: Uses a comparison table in intro to evidence survey gap
Shows structure figure to orient layers and later sections

evidence_locators.claim: States lack of HA security survey covering both attacks and defenses including TAP risks.

raw_headings: II. AN OVERVIEW OF HA SYSTEMS
A. Perception Layer of HA Systems
B. Communication Layer of HA Systems
C. Application Layer of HA Systems
D. General Workflow of HA Systems
section_flow.objective: Lay out HA layered architecture and workflow as baseline for threat analysis.
notable_moves: Places acronym table and architecture figure early for shared vocabulary

evidence_locators.claim: Defines HA layers and TAP workflow with supporting figure/table.

locator.heading: II. AN OVERVIEW OF HA SYSTEMS

section_flow.objective: Compare HA platforms, their rule models, and security policies, forming a taxonomy baseline.
notable_moves: Uses a platform overview table to anchor comparisons of rule/security models

evidence_locators.claim: Summarizes platform architectures and rule/security models with comparison table.

raw_headings: IV. ATTACKS OF HOME AUTOMATION SYSTEMS
section_flow.objective: Classify and detail HA attacks by layer with vulnerability analysis.
key_components: Representative attack vectors and exploited vulnerabilities
notable_moves: Maps attacks directly to the earlier layer model to keep reader aligned

evidence_locators.claim: Details attacks per HA layer and vulnerabilities they exploit.

locator.heading: IV. ATTACKS OF HOME AUTOMATION SYSTEMS

raw_headings: V. DEFENSES OF HOME AUTOMATION SYSTEMS
A. Security Requirements of HA Systems
B. A Taxonomy of Defense Mechanisms
C. Summary and Comparisons of Typical Defenses
section_flow.objective: Identify security requirements and classify defenses for HA systems with comparisons.
notable_moves: Begins with requirements to frame defenses, then provides taxonomy and comparison table

evidence_locators.claim: Defines security requirements and classifies defenses with comparisons.

locator.heading: V. DEFENSES OF HOME AUTOMATION SYSTEMS

section_flow.objective: Highlight open issues for attacks and defenses to guide future research.
key_components: Gaps in attack understanding and modeling
notable_moves: Open issues mirrored to the attack/defense split for continuity

evidence_locators.claim: States open issues for attacks and for defenses separately.

section_flow.objective: Summarize survey and reiterate future direction needs.
notable_moves: Brief conclusion keeps focus on forward look

evidence_locators.claim: Restates scope and future needs succinctly.

hook.evidence: Notes rapid HA adoption and severe security threats amplified by TAP and cross-platform interactions.

gap.evidence: States no survey comprehensively covers HA attacks and defenses including TAP-based risks.

yes_but.evidence: Prior surveys address technology or partial security angles but omit integrated attack-defense view.

contribution.evidence: Lists contributions: layered architecture, attack taxonomy, defense taxonomy, open issues.

scope_boundary.evidence: Focuses on HA system security (attacks and defenses) across perception/communication/application layers.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate HA security gap; lay out layered architecture; compare platforms; classify attacks by layer; classify defenses by requirements; list open issues; conclude.

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Intro/overview use structure and architecture figures plus acronym and comparison tables; platform section uses a large comparison table; attack/defense sections rely on numerous figures per layer and end with summaries.

figures.purpose: show survey structure and HA layered model

tables.purpose: contrast prior HA surveys vs this work
overview of HA platforms and policies

lesson_blocks.lesson: Contrast platform architectures, rule models, and policies to set expectations for threats.
Map attacks to HA layers to keep threat space aligned with architecture.
Start with requirements, then classify defenses and compare implementations.
Revisit the attack/defense split to surface future research gaps.

synthesis.aha_moment: Using the same HA-layer taxonomy for attacks and defenses creates a mirrored structure that simplifies navigation of a broad security space.

style.section_openers_pattern: Open sections by naming the HA layer/topic, then give definitions/examples before taxonomy or lists.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Intro gap with comparison table and structure figure
steps: Quantify HA growth and security risk, emphasizing TAP/cross-platform issues.
Show a comparison table of prior surveys to prove the gap.
List contributions and include a structure figure to preview the layered taxonomy.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Combines evidence of novelty with early navigation aids and shared vocabulary.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Layered baseline before threats
steps: Present the layered architecture (perception/communication/application) and TAP workflow.
Provide an acronym table for clarity.
Use this baseline to anchor subsequent attack/defense mapping.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Sets a clear scaffold that keeps later taxonomies aligned.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Attack taxonomy mirrored to layers
steps: Group attacks by HA layer (perception, communication, application).
For each group, name typical vectors and the vulnerability type.
Use short summaries/figures to keep breadth readable.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Mirrors the system model, making a broad threat space easy to navigate.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Defense taxonomy framed by requirements
steps: Map defenses to HA layers and requirements.
Summarize in a comparison table noting scope and limitations.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Requirements-first framing keeps defenses purposeful and comparable.

conversion_noise: Span tags in headings and table cells
OCR artifacts in tables and symbols

notes: Figure/table counts heuristic; many figures. Math markers likely include inline notation. Conversion left span tags; content otherwise readable.
